name: Flood Tide Vigil
description: Held annually on the last Sunday of August, the Flood Tide Vigil commemorates the catastrophic 2201 Lake Michigan surge event — triggered by a cascade failure in the corponation-managed seawall grid — that submerged four Shelf districts and killed an estimated 11,000 residents over seventy-two hours. Participants float handmade paper lanterns, called 'drift lights,' on any available water surface, from the actual lakefront to puddles in Shelf alleys, and recite the names of the dead from printed or BCI-projected lists. The vigil was organized entirely by survivors and has never received official recognition from any corponation.
cultural_impact: The Flood Tide Vigil has become the most politically charged remembrance in GLMZ, functioning simultaneously as grief ritual and ongoing indictment of the seawall corporations — attendance grows each year as younger generations adopt it as a symbol of systemic corporate neglect.
key_figures: Mama Oksana Delacroix-Nwosu (survivor organizer, now deceased)
Renn Ashikaga (Shelf poet laureate who wrote the Names Litany)
locations: Brackwater Alley, former District 7 flood zone
The Mud Steps, Tier 2 lakeside access ramps
story_hooks: A newly recovered data cache from 2201 contains seawall failure logs that prove the surge was predictable and reported internally three days before it happened — someone has been quietly suppressing this evidence for twenty years.

A synthetic first-responder who worked the 2201 flood rescue has been running the vigil's name-recitation archive alone for years; they've recently discovered names on the list that don't match any human records — suggesting victims no one officially reported.

A Tier 4 executive whose family profited from post-flood redevelopment contracts wants to quietly fund the vigil as 'atonement' — the Drift Collective must decide whether to accept the money, reject it publicly, or use the situation as leverage.
origin_event: The August 2201 Lake Michigan seawall cascade failure, in which corponation infrastructure mismanagement caused a catastrophic surge that destroyed four Shelf districts. Survivors organized the first vigil in August 2202 on the one-year anniversary.
tier_observations: Tier 1 observes with intense communal ceremony — crowds gather at flood-line markers still visible on buildings, names are read aloud for hours, and drift lights cover every water surface. Tier 2 workers who lost family participate solemnly; those without direct connection observe quietly or light a single lantern at home. Tier 3 is broadly aware but participation is low — some make donations to Shelf rebuilding funds. Tier 4 largely ignores it or makes performative charity gestures. Tier 5 corporations treat the date as a minor liability window and keep PR teams on standby.
related_entities: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals Adrenal Phantom Graft — 'The Surge'
